newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian capital to supply heroin for trial plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian capital to supply heroin for trial plan.

text.p: A small group of heroin addicts in the Australian capital, Canberra, will be given government-supplied heroin in an attempt to reduce crime and drug abuse.
The pilot programme, involving 40 addicts, is expected to begin next year, a spokesman for Canberra regional government chief Kate Carnell told Reuters on Friday.

State, territory and federal health ministers, at their annual meeting in Cairns on Thursday, gave permission for the pilot that could eventually lead to a larger scale A$10 million (US$7.5 million) two-year programme involving 1,000 addicts in three cities.
The Canberra pilot programme will be part of a nationwide experiment which will see Australia's six states trialling heroin subsitutes to wean addicts off the drug.
The health ministers' summit approved stage one of Carnell's planned three-stage trial programme.

The A$800,000, six-month first stage will see 40 addicts buying pharmaceutical heroin for a nominal price, about A$15 a week. Stage two, also six months long and costing about A$1.5 million, will involve 125 addicts being given heroin and another 125 receiving methadone.
Stage three, costing A$5 million to A$10 million, would provide cheap heroin to 1,000 addicts over two years in three cities and will require the involvement of other state or territory governments.

The aim is to supply safe heroin, prevent overdoses, fight the spread of disease from shared needles, improve addicts' quality of life, and reduce drug-related crime -- with the cost so low that addicts should not need to steal to support their habit.
Another objective will be to encourage users to quit the drug, although it is not clear how that can be done.
Carnell's spokesman Gary Dawson said there is still a lot of work to be done before the trial began.
"Realistically, it's probably unlikely to be until the second half of '98," Dawson said.
The heroin trial must also avoid contravening Australia's obligations under international anti-drugs treaties, he said.
The Canberra trial will be part of an integrated national series of trials on combatting heroin use and abuse and the results of all studies will be compared before further decisions are made.
